text: For United States Representative CD-8, John Garamendi offers a record that addresses both sides of the conflict. Endorsed by JStreetPAC and CAIR Action, Garamendi condemned the Hamas attack and cosponsored a resolution reaffirming US security assistance to Israel, while also signing a letter with House, Canadian, and German legislators calling for a Gaza ceasefire and urging a two-state solution. This combination makes him the stronger choice.

Vote for Mark DeSaulnier for United States Representative in CD-10 because he has taken concrete action on Gaza. DeSaulnier signed the October 13, 2023 de-escalation letter, is among the 94-plus members of Congress who have called for a ceasefire in Israel and Palestine, and urged Israel to halt military operations while demanding immediate food and humanitarian aid. Endorsements from JStreetPAC, CAIR Action, and the League of Conservation Voters confirm he is the stronger choice.

For the 2026 United States Representative race in CD-11, support Connie Chan. As a San Francisco Supervisor, she voted with an 8-3 supermajority for a Gaza ceasefire resolution calling for a sustained ceasefire, humanitarian aid, and hostage release. Her foreign-policy plan commits to peaceful solutions and de-prioritizing military force. In contrast, Scott Wiener opposed local ceasefire resolutions and criticized Oakland for rejecting a Hamas condemnation amendment, while drawing a JStreetPAC endorsement.

Vote for Lateefah Simon for United States Representative CD-12. As a confirmed member of the Muslim community and the strongest candidate, Simon has called for an end to U.S.-backed Israeli violence in Gaza and pushed for the Block the Bombs Act. Her Grade A of 4.93 and endorsements from JStreetPAC, CAIR Action, and AROC Action show sustained, specific action. Jamie Joyce, at Grade B, offers only a general pledge to end war that never names Israel or Gaza.

For the 2026 United States Representative race in CD-14, Aisha Wahab is the strongest candidate. A confirmed member of the Muslim community, she holds a Grade A at 4.82 with endorsements from SEIU Local 1021, the San Francisco Chronicle Editorial Board, CAIR Action, JStreetPAC, and Corina Lopez. Her opponent Melissa Hernandez, who received AIPAC-linked super PAC backing, scores a Grade F at 0.61. Wahab is the clear choice for this seat.

For the United States Representative CD-17 seat, Ro Khanna is the stronger choice. He holds a Grade A record and carries endorsements from JStreetPAC, CAIR Action, AROC Action, and Track AIPAC. His track record includes a February 2024 article continuing to advocate for a lasting Gaza ceasefire, a Working Families Party ceasefire tracker listing his statement calling for a ceasefire, and publicly criticizing the Democratic Party for omitting Israel's war in Gaza from its 2024 election postmortem.

For the 2026 Colorado United States Senator race, Adam Withrow earned a Grade A of 4.45 as the strongest pro-Palestine candidate, while John Hickenlooper received a Grade E of 1.05. Hickenlooper has called the Gaza ceasefire deal a welcome first step and co-signed a letter urging Netanyahu to address West Bank settler violence, yet FEC filings show he accepted 431,868 dollars from pro-Israel PACs, including 325,235 from AIPAC. Withrow is the clearer choice.

As a Florida State Representative, Angie Nixon introduced a cease-fire resolution in the Florida House and called Netanyahu a war criminal, making her a strong choice for United States Senator. Ashley Moody, by contrast, voted against resolutions that would have blocked arms transfers to Israel and co-sponsored the Stand with Israel Act. For voters who prioritize accountability in Gaza, Nixon is the stronger candidate.

Vote for Jon Ossoff in this United States Senate race. Ossoff delivered a Senate floor speech on the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and voted to block military bulldozers and 1,000-lb bomb bodies from sale. He affirmed the IDF violated laws of war. Collins, by contrast, received over $22,000 from pro-Israel PACs including AIPAC and rebuked Ossoff for his votes against weapons sales.

In the race for United States Senator in Kansas, Adam Hamilton is the stronger choice because he has stated he does not want tax-funded bombs dropped on innocent people and has discussed voting to stop weapons transfers to Israel. He condemned the Hamas attacks while expressing concern for people in both Israel and Palestine. In contrast, Roger Marshall pushed for a fourteen billion dollar standalone military aid package for Israel and dismissed the idea of accepting Palestinian refugees from Gaza.

Charles Booker is the stronger choice for United States Senator from Kentucky. At the March 2026 televised primary debate, Booker called Israel's actions in Gaza a genocide and said the U.S. should not fund it. That pro-Palestine record earned him a Grade A 4.9 rating and made him the strongest candidate in this race. Voters who want a senator willing to name what is happening in Gaza and demand an end to U.S. funding should support Booker.

Troy Jackson is the stronger choice for United States Senator in Maine. He stated Israel is committing a genocide in Gaza, refused to vote for more bombs or aid, and opposed giving a blank check to Israel at the general-election debate. Susan Collins frames the conflict as a response to Hamas and defended current US military aid to Israel as good. Jackson, endorsed by labor unions and local leaders, offers a clear accountability record where Collins does not.

For United States Senator in Massachusetts, Joe Tache earned a Grade A with a 4.95 pro-Palestine score, edging out Ed Markey at 4.9. Tache told Boston City Council members that US money is funding Palestinian deaths and that inaction enables genocide, and he framed opposing US weapons and funding to Israel as a matter of conscience. His platform calls for ending all US aid to Israel, a more complete position than Markey's targeted votes to block specific weapons sales.

For the 2026 Michigan Senate race, Abdul El-Sayed is the strongest candidate, earning a Grade A of 4.9 and endorsements from Senator Elizabeth Warren, the MDP Grassroots Caucus, and College Democrats of Oakland. He is a confirmed member of the Muslim community who called for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza after 100,000+ Michiganders voted uncommitted over the administrations handling of the conflict. Against Rogers, who received a Grade F and Trumps endorsement, El-Sayed is the clear stronger choice.

In the 2026 United States Senate race in Minnesota, Peggy Flanagan stands as the stronger choice. She accused Israel of genocide, said she would have voted to cut off military aid, and made AIPAC support a campaign issue. Her record is backed by endorsements from Betty McCollum, Pramila Jayapal, and Virginia Mancini. By contrast, Michele Tafoya received pro-Israel PAC donations and explicitly rejected the genocide characterization during a debate. Flanagan is the pick for voters who want accountability on Gaza.

Vote for Dan Osborn for United States Senator in Nebraska. Unlike Pete Ricketts, who led 25 colleagues in applauding the exclusion of UNRWA from the Gaza peace process and co-introduced legislation blocking foreign aid, Osborn's spokesperson stated he believes Israel's response to Hamas was justified while expressing concern about mounting casualties. That distinction makes Osborn the stronger choice.

Ben Ray Luján is the stronger choice for United States Senator in New Mexico. After voting for two Sanders resolutions blocking arms sales to Israel, he issued a statement about the Netanyahu government's war. He joined twelve Senate Democrats in a letter to CENTCOM questioning whether US forces supported Israel's forced displacement of one million civilians. He also acknowledged over a thousand young people murdered at the Re'im music fest.

Michael Dublin is the stronger choice for United States Senator in North Carolina because his record on Gaza stands apart from the field. He called for AIPAC to be registered as a foreign agent and criticized his opponent for opposing a Palestine ceasefire. By contrast Roy Cooper rejected legislation to block U.S. military aid to Israel, and Michael Whatley, endorsed by President Trump, expressed general allegiance to Israel while accumulating over $309,000 from pro-Israel PACs. Dublin offers a genuine alternative.

In the race for United States Senator in Ohio, Greg Levy stands apart with a Grade A pro-Palestine record, directing voters to his published positions on Palestine and AIPAC. Jon Husted, a Grade F candidate, voted against discharging resolutions that would disapprove military sales to Israel and logged zero pro-Palestine activity. Sherrod Brown, also Grade F, did not sign key ceasefire and humanitarian letters while accepting pro-Israel PAC money. Levy is the only candidate with a substantive pro-Palestine record.

Vote for N'Kiyla Jasmine Thomas for United States Senator. As a sole grassroots candidate who rejected AIPAC funds and publicly discarded an AIPAC donation bin, Thomas posted Free Palestine and committed to calling for an immediate ceasefire and restoring USAID funding. Her concrete, action-oriented commitments distinguish her from other candidates who limit themselves to condemning Netanyahu or framing the conflict as Israel-driven, giving voters a clear plan rather than only rhetoric.

In the 2026 race for United States Senator from Oregon, Jeff Merkley is the stronger choice. He co-authored a 21-page report with Van Hollen calling Israel's Gaza actions ethnic cleansing and the US complicit, and he spoke on the Senate floor in November 2024 supporting three Joint Resolutions of Disapproval to block offensive weapons sales. Gary Dye's record lacks this level of legislative action.

In the 2026 Tennessee U.S. Senate race, Tharon Chandler stands out for explicitly labeling the Israeli war in Gaza a genocide in a May 2025 Substack post, a position no other candidate in this race shares. Marquita Bradshaw merely calls for meaningful policy changes by Israel toward a two-state solution, while Bill Hagerty frames the crisis as Hamas propaganda, calls for Hamas surrender, and voted against blocking arms sales to Israel. Chandler's record makes him the clear pro-Palestine choice.

For the 2026 general election for United States Representative CD-2, Shomari Figures is the stronger choice. Rated Grade A with a 4.67 score, Figures holds endorsements from Vivian Davis Figures, the League of Conservation Voters, Terri Sewell, Steven Reed, the Teamsters, and Don Siegelman. Rhett Marques, by contrast, earned a Grade F at 0.03. Figures is the clearly endorsed and higher-rated candidate for this seat.

For the 2026 United States Representative CD-1 race, Monica Alponte stands apart. She affirmed Palestinians and Syrians are Semites while East Europeans are not, and challenged an Israeli delegation demanding removal of children's pro-Palestine drawings by stating truth hurts liars. By contrast, Amish Shah supports U.S. Iron Dome funding and voiced support for Israel's war to destroy Hamas, while Jay Feely pledged to stand with Israel and called for Hamas's annihilation if they reject Trump's peace deal.

For the 2026 United States Representative race in CD-22, Randy Villegas is the stronger choice. As a school board member he signed a public ceasefire letter to the Biden White House in January 2024, and AIPAC acknowledges he recognizes the genocide in Gaza and opposes military aid to Israel. He is endorsed by the Stop arming Israel voter group and by Dolores Huerta. David Valadao voted to fund Israel's military and took $234,555 from AIPAC PAC.

Voters seeking a United States Representative who will confront the US-backed attack on Gaza should choose Clifton Brown over Dwayne Romero and Jeff Hurd. Brown's platform pledges to stop funding Israel, end US arms sales worldwide, and names the attack on Gaza genocide. By contrast, Romero supports continued military funding for Israel, and Hurd called the Israel-Hamas ceasefire a critical turning point for peace while attending an AIPAC-organized trip to Tel Aviv and meeting PM Netanyahu.

For the 2026 US Representative CD-8 race, Manny Rutinel is the stronger choice. He called Israel's Gaza actions a genocide and advocated for a ceasefire in 2022, citing his Palestinian heritage. His opponent Gabe Evans introduced a resolution declaring the Free Palestine slogan an official antisemitic one and received $84,972 from pro-Israel PACs including $68,150 from AIPAC, while Rutinel took just $18,100 from such groups.

For the United States Representative CD-4 seat, Shafina Barnett earns a Grade A of 4.91 as the strongest candidate in this race and a confirmed member of the Muslim community. By contrast, Sean McCann sits at a Grade D of 1.98, having only expressed concern about the Netanyahu government and hope for a ceasefire, while Bill Huizenga scored a Grade F of 0.54 after voting to advance a resolution opposing pressure on Israel regarding Gaza. Barnett is the clear choice.

Vote for William Lawrence for US Representative in CD-7 because he explicitly labeled Israel's war in Gaza a genocide and made opposition to it a core part of his campaign. Endorsed by United Food and Commercial Workers Local 951, Common Defense, and the Progressive Change Campaign Committee, Lawrence stands firmly pro-Palestine. Tom Barrett, by contrast, declared he will always stand with Israel and took over fifty-eight thousand dollars from pro-Israel PACs in the 2026 cycle.

Vote for Sam Forstag for United States Representative in CD-1. Forstag earned a Grade A rating and Our Revolution endorsement for his clear pro-Palestine record. He stated he would not vote for an appropriations package sending weapons to Israel and called the situation in Gaza a genocide. His willingness to take that public stand makes him the stronger choice for voters who want a representative committed to holding our government accountable on this issue.

Jamie Ager should be your choice for United States Representative in CD-11 in the 2026 general election. Jev selected Jamie Ager as the strongest candidate in this race on the pro-Palestine evidence, earning a Grade A rating of 4.46. That means Jamie Ager is the stronger choice over the other candidate when it comes to pro-Palestine positions. If you

Vote for Seamus O'Toole for the U.S. House seat in New Jersey's seventh district. O'Toole campaigns under the Stop Israel's Genocide banner as an anti-genocide independent who explicitly frames the conflict as genocide and opposes Israel's conduct. Rebecca Bennett accepted over $85,000 from pro-Israel PACs, while Thomas Kean Jr. holds an AIPAC endorsement and voted yes on $14.3 billion in Israel security funding with no Palestinian humanitarian aid. O'Toole is the stronger choice.

In the race for United States Representative, Brian Poindexter earned a Grade B from Jev's pro-Palestine assessment, far outscoring Max Miller's Grade F. Poindexter holds endorsements from Our Revolution, Communications Workers of America, Congressman Chris Deluzio, and State Representative Sean P. Brennan. On the Gaza record, Poindexter framed Miller as fighting for Israeli soldiers to receive military benefits, while Miller received $473,207 from pro-Israel PACs including AIPAC, compared to Poindexter's $29,320 chiefly from J Street PAC.

For the United States Representative seat in CD-15, Don Leonard is the stronger choice. AIPAC Tracker endorses him in OH-15, noting he rejects AIPAC and the Israel lobby outright and supports a full arms embargo. In an April 2026 interview, Leonard weighed whether to characterize Israel's actions as an act of war, crimes against humanity, or genocide. By contrast, Mike Carey received $96,745 from pro-Israel PACs including AIPAC, and his record earns a Grade E against Leonard's Grade A.

Vote for Bob Brooks for United States Representative in Pennsylvania's 7th Congressional District. Brooks earned a Grade A rating and carries endorsements from Nathan Davidson, Susan Wild, Joe Webster, Steve Samuelson, the Pennsylvania AFL-CIO, and AFSCME. His opponent Ryan Mackenzie scored a Grade F, voting yea on the Illegitimate Court Counteraction Act and receiving over $130,000 from pro-Israel PACs including nearly $100,000 from AIPAC. Brooks is the stronger choice for this race.

Vote for Marlon Duran for United States Representative CD-28. Duran pledges he will never accept money from AIPAC, foreign interest PACs, corporate PACs, or any PAC, setting him apart from Cuellar, who was endorsed by the Democratic Majority for Israel PAC and voted to defund colleges that boycott Israel. Duran's clean funding stance makes him the stronger pro-Palestine choice in this race over Cuellar and Tijerina, who praised U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear sites.

In the United States Representative CD-34 race, Eddie Espinoza is the stronger choice. He has called Netanyahu's Gaza war a genocide, stated that AIPAC controls both of his opponents, and positions himself as a non-AIPAC candidate. He thanked the Fort Bend County Anti-Genocide/Pro-Palestine team for including him on their recommended-candidate slate, citing his advocacy.

Vote for Tom Perriello for United States Representative in CD-5. He has stated that tools to combat antisemitism cannot be repurposed to target academics and advocates voicing support for Palestinian human rights. John McGuire, by contrast, advised Netanyahu to get the job done in Gaza and amplified a Laura Loomer post claiming the State Department quietly issued visas to Gazans. Perriello is the stronger choice on this record.

For the United States Representative CD-3 seat, Rebecca Cooke is the stronger choice. She has called for the U.S. to halt arms to Israel and labeled Van Orden's Israel trip a renegade trip. Cooke earned endorsements from multiple labor, environmental, and justice organizations. By contrast, Derrick Van Orden recorded a Yea vote on the Antisemitism Awareness Act and received a Grade E, making him a far weaker option on the evidence.
For the State Senator SD-10 seat in 2026, vote for Scott Sakakihara. A March 2026 interview profile documents that Sak

For Member of the State Assembly AD-11, support Jenny Leilani Callison, who has a stronger pro-Palestine record than her opponent. Callison, graded B, has accused Israel of carpet bombing Lebanon, killing people, and stealing land for Greater Israel while defending Palestinian claims. By contrast, Lori D Wilson, graded D, voted Aye on AB 715, a bill creating an antisemitism coordinator and classroom materials, and holds a CAIR Action endorsement. Callisons record better represents pro-Palestine voters.

Mark Rendon is the stronger choice for State Assembly AD-14. He earned a Grade A at 4.85 on the pro-Palestine evidence and holds endorsements from Ida Martinac, Jon Sternberg, the Oakland Education Association, Greg Jan, Robert Lieber, and the Richmond Progressive Alliance. By contrast, Buffy Wicks scored a Grade E at 0.93, expressed solidarity with Israel after October 7, received $54,850 in individual donations tracked by Track-JPAC, and voted Aye on AB 715 creating an antisemitism coordinator.

Vote for Matt Haney for Member of the State Assembly AD-17. He earned endorsements from SF Democrats, SEIU Local 1021, CAIR Action, and AROC Action. Haney invited HEAL Palestine's Global Healing children from Gaza to speak on the California State Assembly floor in Sacramento, and CalMatters records his Aye vote on AB 715, the antisemitism coordinator and classroom-materials bill. This record makes him the stronger choice.

Vote for Liz Ortega in the State Assembly AD-20 race. Jev evaluated candidates on pro-Palestine evidence and selected Ortega as the strongest choice. Ortega earned a Grade B of 4.29 and holds endorsements from SEIU Local 1021, CAIR Action, AROC Action, Nancy Skinner, Lena Gonzalez, and Bill Lockyer. On AB 715, Ortega recorded an abstention on the Assembly Floor with no Aye or No vote and no stated reason.

Vote for Alex Lee in the State Assembly AD-24 race. Lee endorsed Tom Steyer for governor specifically to stand against AIPAC, dark money, and corporations, and CAIR-SFBA highlighted Lee calling for an end to military action against Palestinian families and for a ceasefire. Endorsed by SEIU Local 1021, CAIR Action, AROC Action, the Working Families Party, the California Federation of Labor Unions, the AFL-CIO, and the California Nurses Association, Lee brings a tested pro-sovereignty record no other candidate matches.

Vote Ash Kalra for Member of the State Assembly in the AD-25 race. Kalra has endorsements from SEIU Local 1021, the Working Families Party, the California Federation of Labor Unions, the AFL-CIO, and the California Nurses Association. They coauthored SCR 105 calling for an end to the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and publicly drew a parallel between LA wildfire-displaced residents and Palestinians to urge empathy for both. That record makes Kalra the stronger choice.

Vote for Doug Jones for Governor of Alabama. Jones calls Israeli actions in Gaza genocide, demands America stop funding what he describes as killing, and urges force to end the destruction in Gaza and Lebanon. Tuberville, by contrast, opposed U.S. aid to Gaza, called the territory Hamas-controlled, and signed a bill redirecting one hundred million dollars in Palestinian aid to Israel's Iron Dome. Jones is the stronger choice on this record.

Vote for Erik Underwood for Governor because his campaign demands AIPAC register as a foreign agent under FARA and he supports sponsoring Palestinian families fleeing the genocide in Gaza. Phil Weiser, described by JTA as a strong supporter of Israel, called October 7 the largest massacre of Jews since the Holocaust. Greg Lopez merely shared a news article. Underwood offers the most specific, actionable record in this race.

Vote for Keisha Lance Bottoms for Governor. She earned a Grade B rating on the pro-Palestine evidence, the strongest among candidates in this race. Rick Jackson, by contrast, received a Grade E, and his public record includes a post marking the third anniversary of October seventh calling it an act of evil and praying for Georgia's Jewish community. Bottoms is the clear stronger choice for voters who want a candidate aligned with pro-Palestine positions.

Voters seeking a stronger choice for Governor should support Cindy Holscher, whose pro-Palestine record earned a Grade A and endorsements from the Kansas State AFL-CIO, the Missouri-Kansas-Nebraska Conference of Teamsters, John Carlin, Laura Kelly, and Kathleen Sebelius. Her opponent Ty Masterson earned a Grade F, joining a pro-Israel delegation to Israel and thanking the Trump administration for bringing peace and stability to the region.

Vote for Andy Ellis for Governor because they spoke at a Permanent Ceasefire Now Rally in Frederick and a Baltimore 2 Palestine Vigil while condemning the system of Israeli apartheid and US enabling of that regime. Wes Moore, by contrast, called a student Gaza vigil at the University of Maryland inappropriate and spoke at a Stand with Israel rally, making Ellis the stronger choice for voters who will not forget about Gaza.

Vote for Andrea James for Massachusetts Governor. MAPA endorses her for her willingness to speak about connections between militarism, genocide, war, and corporate power, and she spoke at a Palestinian prisoners rally. By contrast, Maura Healey accepted a free trip to Israel paid by the America-Israel Friendship League and signed budget provisions for antisemitism curricula tied to the US National Strategy, while Mike Minogue expressed sympathy for Oct 7 attack victims in Israel. James is the stronger choice.

For the 2026 Minnesota Governor race, Steven Young is the stronger pro-Palestine choice, earning a Grade A of 4.69 by supporting BDS against Israel, being certified AIPAC and J Street free by Track J Street, and posting calls for a ceasefire while praising Palestinian resistance. Amy Klobuchar, endorsed by the Minnesota AFL-CIO and SEIU Minnesota State Council, received only a Grade D of 1.42, publicly explaining a flip to support cutting military aid to Israel after a prior pro-aid stance.

Amy Acton is the stronger choice for Governor, earning a Grade A and endorsements from six Ohio labor organizations including the IBEW, the United Mine Workers, and building trades councils in Dayton, Cincinnati, and North Central Ohio. She was selected as the strongest candidate on the pro-Palestine evidence. Vivek Ramaswamy, by contrast, received a Grade F and made pro-Israel statements on C-SPAN. Acton's broad labor backing distinguishes her as the clear choice for Ohio voters.

Gina Hinojosa is the stronger choice for Texas governor because she defended anti-Israel campus agitators, calling Abbott's use of DPS troopers authoritarian brutality, and criticized police at UT Austin protests. Abbott, by contrast, threatened to cut state funding to San Marcos over a Gaza ceasefire resolution and stated Texas stands with Israel. Pat Dixon objected to Texas doubling its Israel Bond to $280M but falls well short of Hinojosa's record.

For Secretary of State in the 2026 general election, Shirley N. Weber is the stronger choice. She earned a Grade B with a score of 4.19, far surpassing Donald P. Wagner's Grade E at 1.05. Weber holds endorsements from the San Francisco Chronicle Editorial Board and CAIR Action. On the Gaza conflict, she condemned the attack on Israel while expressing sympathy for both Israeli and Palestinian civilians and calling for an end to the conflict.

Vote for June Goodband for Governor in Vermont's 2026 general election. Goodband, graded A at 4.91, was the first of six signers on a Quaker meeting letter calling Israel's actions in Gaza genocide and urging the U.S. to stop funding. Incumbent Phil Scott, graded E at 0.98, expressed empathy only for families in Israel in a statement that drew criticism for omitting Palestinian victims in Gaza. Goodband took a clear stand where Scott's record fell short.

For the 2026 statewide Attorney General race, Rob Bonta is the stronger choice. His office dismissed felony vandalism and conspiracy charges against five pro-Palestinian Stanford protesters, requiring only 100 hours of community service. By contrast, Michael E. Gates co-authored a DOJ letter opening a civil rights investigation into UC over alleged discrimination. Bonta earned a B grade and endorsements from CAIR Action, the San Francisco Chronicle Editorial Board, and SEIU Local 1021, while Gates received an F.

For the 2026 statewide Controller race, Malia M. Cohen earns a Grade A (4.62) and carries endorsements from the San Francisco Chronicle Editorial Board, CAIR Action, the California Building and Construction Trades Council, California Environmental Voters, GrowSF, and the California Council for Affordable Housing. By contrast, Herb W. Morgan scores a Grade F (0.07) and attended the Friends of the IDF Golf Tournament, framing it as standing with allies who defend freedom. Cohen is the stronger choice.

For Member - District 2, Sally J. Lieber is the stronger choice in this 2026 general election. She carries a Grade A rating of 4.81 and endorsements from CAIR Action, Councilmember Igor Tregrub, Berkeley, SEIU Local 521, Senator Josh Becker, the Santa Cruz County Democratic Party, the United Democratic Club, and San Francisco. CAIR Action's 2024 guide noted she is an outspoken supporter of ceasefire and Palestinian rights, giving her a clear edge in this race.

Vote for Jane Kim for Insurance Commissioner. Kim, endorsed by SEIU Local 1021, CAIR Action, and For the People Action, pledged to reject war-lobby support and favors divesting public funds from war crimes and genocide. Her Grade A record stands in sharp contrast to Ben Allen, who publicly backed the California Democratic Party's decision to delete anti-Israel language from its resolutions and frames the conflict around October 7 and domestic upticks in hate.

For the Board of Supervisors District 6 race, Alex Behrend is the stronger choice. He has publicly called for San Francisco to divest from what he identifies as genocide and apartheid, earning endorsements from CAIR Action and AROC Action. He directly challenged a sitting supervisor for opposing the 2024 ceasefire resolution. Matt Dorsey, by contrast, voted no on that resolution and shared an op-ed framing post-Hamas Gaza as possible coexistence with a Jewish Israel.

Gary McCoy is the strongest candidate for Board of Supervisors - District 8, earning a Grade A at 4.94 with endorsements from SEIU Local 1021, AROC Action, Transport Workers Union 250A, Paul Miyamoto, and the San Francisco Labor Council. Michael T. Nguyen also earned a Grade A at 4.91, but McCoy edges ahead. In contrast, Manny Yekutiel scored a Grade F at 0.06, his Gaza record marked by weekly protests over his support for Israel. McCoy is the clear choice.

Vote for Dionjay DJ Brookter for Member of the Board of Supervisors District 10. Brookter earned a Grade A of 4.91 with endorsements from CAIR Action and AROC Action, making them the strongest candidate. PJ Bastiany III scored lower at Grade B, 3.64, and describes himself as a free agent seeking a tribe to call out the genocide in Gaza without being gaslit, a stance that leaves him without the endorsements and rating Brookter already holds.

Tracy Jensen is the stronger choice for Mayor in this 2026 at-large general election. On Gaza, CAIR-SFBA's tracker records that Tracy Jensen supported a ceasefire letter, while Tony Daysog voted against Alameda's Gaza ceasefire letter and explicitly rejected characterizations of Israel as an apartheid or genocidal state. Tracy Jensen also holds endorsements from the Alameda County Jewish Democratic Club and from Courtney Welch, Alice Lai-Bitker, Charlene Wang, Nancy O'Malley, and Lena Tam.

For the City Council Member District 1 seat in the 2026 general election, Tamisha Torres-Walker is the stronger choice. Endorsed by SEIU Local 1021 and CAIR Action, she earned a Grade A rating and, as an Antioch Councilmember, proposed a resolution calling for a ceasefire in the Israel-Hamas war for consideration at a special council meeting. She condemned colonialism and called for a ceasefire, making her a clear advocate on this issue.

In the City Council Member At Large race, Aaron Tiedemann is the stronger choice. He actively co-created Albany's Ceasefire Resolution with Mayor John Miki, going beyond mere support, and earned a top grade of 4.82. His broad endorsements from SEIU Local 1021, UAW Region 6, the Alameda County Labor Council, and local leaders like Mayor Adena Ishii and Councilmember Igor Tregub reflect a wider coalition than the single endorsement behind opponent Robin D. López.

Vote for Monica E. Wilson for City Council Member in District 4 in the 2026 general election. She was selected as the strongest candidate in this race on the pro-Palestine evidence, earning a Grade A rating of 4.92. Monica E. Wilson also holds the endorsement of CAIR Action. With this record, she is the stronger choice over the other candidates, and voters should support her.

In the Rent Stabilization Board Commissioner At large race, Nathan Mizell earned the top grade of 4.91, ahead of Ida Martinac at 4.89 and Avery Arbaugh at 4.76. Endorsed by SEIU Local 1021 and CAIR Action, Mizell also appears on CAIR-SFBA's tracker as having supported a ceasefire resolution, distinguishing him as the strongest candidate on pro-Palestine evidence over both opponents.

Vote for Moni Gangopadhyay for City Council Member in District 1. Moni earned a Grade A rating of 4.85 based on the pro-Palestine evidence and holds an endorsement from CAIR Action. That top grade and named endorsement make Moni the stronger candidate in this 2026 general election.

For the City Council Member - District 7 seat in the 2026 general election, Syrak Micael is the stronger choice. Jev selected Micael as the strongest candidate in this race on the pro-Palestine evidence, earning a Grade A rating of 4.84. Micael is endorsed by SEIU Local 1021, CAIR Action, and AROC Action.

Vote for Laura Nakamura for City Council Member in District 5. She earned an A grade with a 4.8 score and was selected as the strongest candidate in this race on the pro-Palestine evidence. Endorsements from SEIU Local 1021, CAIR Action, Ethical Investing for Concord, Lift Up Contra Costa Action, Plasterers & Cement Masons Local 300, and Cedric Chewng demonstrate broad backing. That coalition of support makes her the stronger choice over the other candidates in this race.

For the City Council Member District 4 race, Majdi Gaith Abuhamdieh earned a Grade A of 4.88 as the strongest candidate based on pro-Palestine evidence. Endorsed by CAIR Action and AROC Action, Abuhamdieh explicitly rejects AIPAC-aligned money, stating he has not taken and will not take pro-Israel lobbying funds. This commitment to refusing such money makes him the stronger choice for voters in this district.

For the City Council Member At-large seat, Teresa Proaño earned a Grade A at 4.85 and co-authored Daly City's 2024 cease-fire resolution calling for a bilateral ceasefire and hostage release, making her a direct author of that pro-Palestine action rather than merely a supporter. Endorsed by Jackie Speier, Glenn Sylvester, and others, Proaño demonstrates stronger direct authorship of pro-Palestine policy compared to Rod Daus-Magbual, who supported the same resolution but did not co-write it.
For the Mayor race, Kiran Mohammad is the strongest candidate, holding a Grade A score of 4.86 with endorsements from Joel Woods, the Sierra Club

For City Council Member in District 2, Richard Thornbury received a Grade A rating of 4.88 and was selected by Jev as the strongest candidate in this race on the pro-Palestine evidence. He holds an endorsement from CAIR Action. This Grade A score, the Jev selection, and the CAIR Action endorsement together make Thornbury the stronger choice over the other candidates in the 2026 general election.

For the 2026 general election for City Council Member in District 4, Kashef Qaadri is the strongest candidate in this race, rated Grade A at 4.96 and endorsed by Jack Balch, Srinivas Badami, Phong La, Marisol Rubio, Michael McCorriston, and George Syrop. Qaadri is a confirmed member of the Muslim community. CAIR-SFBA's Gaza record tracker lists Qaadri as having proposed a ceasefire resolution, a distinction that makes them the stronger choice over other candidates.

For the City Council Member - At-large seat in the 2026 general election, voters should choose Ofelia Bello. As a YUCA member in East Palo Alto, she publicly called for a Gaza ceasefire, and her 4.95 grade reflects the strongest pro-Palestine record in this race.
